newsitem.title: UK: Dollar recovers in Europe but finds upside tough.
newsitem.headline: Dollar recovers in Europe but finds upside tough.

text.p: The dollar clawed back lost ground against the mark and the yen in Europe but failed to make major headway as the mark rose off its worst levels on the European crosses and against the yen, traders said.
Offers around 1.5150 marks capped the dollar's upside, denting traders' expectations it would take out a sticky barrier at 1.5160 marks, a key support level from last week.

"The dollar is once again in a pattern defined by solid support on the downside and difficulty in overcoming resistance on the upside, which is keeping it in a neutral mode," said Teis Knuthsen, international economist at First Chicago in London.

At 1531 GMT the dollar was at 1.5138/41 marks, up from 1.5066/76 in late European trading on Wednesday. Bids in the 1.5060/50 area helped the dollar to bounce back during its sharp downturn earlier this week, traders said.
Against the yen, the dollar stood at 113.78/88 yen, up from a Far Eastern low at around 113.20 and little changed from the previous European close at 113.82/87.

While dollar/mark looks set to remain stuck in a narrow range, traders were confident dollar/yen's downmove was a mere blip in a healthy uptrend, seeing no reasons for outflows of yield-thirsty Japanese capital to dry up.
An eleventh-hour attack of nerves ahead of next week's U.S. election sparked overnight profit-taking on the dollar.

"The main driving force behind this currency pair is Japanese investors and their need to invest abroad to enhance yield, and we see this continuing," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko Europe in London.

Mark/yen, which has dominated dollar/yen of late, recovered from a low of 74.90 yen to trade at 75.15/18 in late Europe, down a 3 1/2 year high at 75.87 on Wednesday and from 75.54/56 in late trading here on Wednesday. Traders said the recovery back above 75 was crucial in maintaining mark/yen's uptrend.
But with U.S. non-farm payrolls for October on Friday looming over the foreign exchange market, movements are expected to be fairly muted ahead of the release at 1330 GMT on Friday.

Payrolls are forecast to show a rise of 212,000 against the 40,000 decline last month. Economists said the market's current yield-fixation means the dollar should react to the figures' interest rate implications rather than asset markets' response.

A slew of U.S. data on Thursday had little impact. September personal income rose 0.6 percent, while spending rose just 0.1 versus forecasts for a rise of 0.6 and O.3 percent respectively. Weekly jobless claims rose to 342,000 from 319,000.
The Chicago PMI rose rose to 56.9 from 56.3, way above the 54.0 reading forecast by economists.

The mark had a choppy day against the French franc. It was it after the European Commission said it had cleared France's transfer of 37.5 billion francs from France Telecom to the national budget. France sees the transfer as vital in cutting its deficit to the target of three percent of GDP in its quest to join the single European currency.
A 5 basis points cut in the French intervention rate to 3.20 percent, meanwhile, had little impact on the franc. Many traders had expected a larger reduction of ten basis points.
There had been market fears that the Commission would disallow the French plan, designed to help cut the budget deficit in order to qualify for European monetary union.
Mark/French franc was at 3.3754/59, little changed from 3.3765/69 but off an intraday low at 3.3733.
French unemployment remained at a record high of 12.6 percent in September.

Sterling took a breather from its sharp rise in the wake of a surprise UK interest rate rise on Wendesday. It ended little changed from late Wednesday at 2.4630/40 marks. Cable was at $1.6262/72 from $1.6322/32. --Astrid Zweynert +44 171 542 7792
